_meta.conventions: "unknown" = not verified from a source during research. Values marked (unverified) come from a single third-party/retailer page. Spec figures are per the cited sources and vary by hardware model; always confirm in the vendor tool. Framework 'Qt5' etc. is only stated where a source confirmed it.
_meta.uiaNotes: Win32/WinForms/WPF expose good UI Automation trees. Qt5 exposes UIA only if its accessibility plugin is active (Qt >= 5.x Windows UIA backend) and custom-painted widgets (graphs, knobs) are usually opaque. Adobe/Harman AIR apps expose almost nothing to UIA. HTML5/Electron/CEF apps expose a UIA tree via Chromium accessibility (needs --force-renderer-accessibility or a screen-reader flag).

vendors.software: miniDSP plugins (per product, e.g. C-DSP 8x12 / 2x4 HD plugin) and miniDSP Device Console (DC, newer HTML5 platform, started with Flex Eight); Dirac Live for DL models
vendors.version: unknown (plugins rebuilt on Harman AIR SDK; Device Console changelog at minidsp.com/support/device-console-changelog)
vendors.framework: Legacy plugins: Adobe AIR (now Harman AIR SDK builds). Device Console: HTML5-based.
vendors.connection: USB (HID control for 2x4 HD: VID 0x2752 / PID 0x0011); optional WI-DG WiFi on some models; TCP 5333 via minidsp-rs server
vendors.presetFormat: miniDSP project/config file (XML, per forum reports); PEQ biquad text import ('biquad1, b0=..., b1=..., b2=..., a1=..., a2=...,')
vendors.api: No official API, but reverse-engineered USB HID protocol implemented by open-source minidsp-rs (Rust CLI + TCP server on port 5333 + HTTP API) covering master gain/mute/source/preset, input/output gain, routing, PEQ biquad import, crossover biquads, delay, FIR, compressor, invert. Caveat: official plugin cannot read back filter/delay changes made by third-party tools.
vendors.downloadUrl: https://www.minidsp.com/ (User Downloads section, login with serial) ; minidsp-rs releases: https://github.com/mrene/minidsp-rs/releases
vendors.peqBands: 2x4 HD: 10 PEQ per output (official manual); input PEQ also present. Other models vary.
vendors.delayUnits: ms (exact max per model unknown; a miniDSP comparison table cites up to 7.5 ms for some products)
vendors.crossoverTypes: Butterworth, Linkwitz-Riley (2x4 HD manual); crossover blocks are 2 groups x 4 biquads so arbitrary biquad crossovers are possible
vendors.slopes: unknown exact list (up to 48 dB/oct per miniDSP comparison table; 4 biquads per side = up to 8th order)
vendors.notes: Best candidate for a native integration: open-source, tested protocol, biquad-level control, must be sample-rate aware (2x4 HD runs 96 kHz; C-DSP 8x12 sample rate unverified). Device-specific: supported list in minidsp-rs README includes 2x4HD, Flex, DDRC-24, DDRC-88A/D, miniSHARC, 2x8/8x8/4x10/10x10, nanoDIGI 2x8, SHD series, C-DSP 8x12 v2. REW 'Save filter coefficients' must match device sample rate and number of biquads. Dirac Live models (C-DSP 8x12 DL) are tuned via Dirac, not exposed by minidsp-rs.

vendors.software: DSP PC-Tool (V4 / V5 / V6)
vendors.version: 5.07.01 (22.11.2024, listed 'Last release' on EN download page); DSP PC-Tool 6 announced (EISA 2025-2026 award) - exact build unknown
vendors.framework: Qt 5 + MinGW, 32-bit (static analysis of 4.80b by helix-unwound); V5/V6 unknown
vendors.connection: USB virtual COM port: CDC-ACM (usbser.sys, VID 0x2E4F, PIDs 0x2000-0x3006) on newer units, FTDI VCP on older (e.g. DSP PRO MK2); QSerialPort 8N1 at 19200 with high-baud switch (230400/250000). App links Qt5Bluetooth and Qt5Network (WiFi control on newer units).
vendors.presetFormat: *.afpx (current) / *.afp (previous) setup files; device parameter map *.at01 (qCompress+zlib of SigmaStudio header) and *.AF1 (hex text) inside installer. Format not documented.
vendors.api: None official. Serial framing partially reverse-engineered statically (TX: 0x42|L|~L|ch|payload|sum8; RX: 0x43...) by helix-unwound - NOT verified on hardware. Host computes biquads and writes SigmaDSP parameter RAM.
vendors.peqBands: unknown per current model (reviews of older Helix units cite 30/31-band EQ per channel)
vendors.qRange: unknown (older P-DSP: crossover Q 0.2-2.0 in self-define mode, forum)
vendors.delayUnits: cm/ms in tool (older units: 7 mm increments per forum)
vendors.crossoverTypes: Butterworth, Bessel, Chebyshev, Linkwitz-Riley, user-defined (older-unit reviews; confirm in V5/V6)
vendors.slopes: 6-30 dB/oct in 6 dB steps on older units (reviews); newer units likely more - unknown
vendors.notes: Most popular high-end car DSP family in EU; one tool covers ~30 BRAX/HELIX/MATCH models, so one UIA profile pays off widely. REW Generic EQ import is supported (helix-unwound findings) -> hybrid route: FalseAudio writes a REW-format filter text file and drives the PC-Tool import dialog via UIA, then sets crossovers/delays via UIA. Qt5 custom widgets may be opaque to UIA; plan for coordinate/keyboard fallback. Native protocol is possible long-term but unverified and risky (writes to DSP RAM).

vendors.software: bit Drive (bit One HD / bit One HD Virtuoso / bit Ten / bit Nine etc.), incl. ACCORDO auto-tune in bit Drive 2.0; legacy bit Tune (measurement kit)
vendors.version: bit Drive 2.0 (announced July 2024); Virtuoso software v3.0 (Jan 2022)
vendors.connection: USB (micro-USB on bit One HD); AC Link bus for remotes/DRC
vendors.presetFormat: unknown (offline-mode project files exist; 8 memories on device)
vendors.peqBands: bit One HD (Virtuoso) spec sheet: 13 outputs, 13 poles IIR per output (+12/-15 dB), or 9 FIR + 3 IIR in FIR mode; AUX/optical inputs 10 poles. ACCORDO target-curve EQ: 11 bands.
vendors.delayUnits: ms / cm / inch: 0-22 ms, step 0.04 ms (1.4 cm, 0.6 in)
vendors.slopes: Linkwitz 12/24/36/48; Butterworth 6-48 (6 dB steps); Bessel 6-36; FIR 6-48 dB/oct
vendors.notes: bit Drive 2.0 imports EQ filter settings from REW (format not stated) and has built-in ACCORDO auto-tune using one external mic or soundcard. Route: UIA for crossovers/delay + REW-filter import dialog for EQ. customDRC only reverse-engineers the DRC remote hardware (AC Link), not the PC protocol. Hertz H8 DSP and Audison Prima bit amps likely use bit Drive-family software (unverified).

vendors.software: Prima AP bit configuration software (AP8.9 bit, AP F8.9 bit); Hertz H8 DSP software - unknown
vendors.notes: Windows-based with configuration wizard and offline mode. importsREW=false means not verified, not confirmed absent.

vendors.notes: Windows XP-10 only per Focal; old, unmaintained. Coarse 0.1 ms delay.

vendors.software: KENWOOD DSP Control (mobile app)

vendors.software: Dayton Audio DSP-408 Windows app; 'Dayton Audio DSP Control' mobile app
vendors.connection: USB-B for PC (USB HID, envelope 80 80 80 ee); Bluetooth classic RFCOMM/SPP via DSP-BT4.0/5.0 dongle (USB-A port carries SPI, not USB)
vendors.presetFormat: Vendor backup files (format decoded by dsp408-tuner; 296-byte channel records) - not officially documented
vendors.api: No official API, but protocol fully reverse-engineered and validated on hardware: dsp408-py (USB HID: volume, mute, delay, invert, routing, crossover, 10-band PEQ, preset save, firmware flash) and dsp408-tuner (Bluetooth RFCOMM; closed-loop auto-tune with rollback).
vendors.peqBands: 10 PEQ per output channel (80 total); forum mentions 2 shelf types available among them
vendors.qRange: 0.404 - 28.85 ('RBJ Q / half-gain' per Dayton tech support); gain -12..+12 dB in 0.1 dB; on the wire bandwidth quantized 0.01 oct/step
vendors.delayUnits: ms / cm / in in UI; wire value is integer samples at 48 kHz, 0-391 samples (~8.147 ms, 0-277 cm). dsp408-py reports cap 359 taps.
vendors.notes: Two ADAU1701 SigmaDSPs at fixed 48 kHz. Every write is immediately non-volatile, no undo - snapshot before write. Very popular budget car DSP; the same OEM platform may be rebadged elsewhere (t.racks DSP 408 is a DIFFERENT device with network protocol: Aeternitaas/dsp-408-ui). REW export: use 10 filters, 48 kHz, Q range above.

vendors.connection: USB HID control transfers (VID 0x8888 / PID 0x1234, 256-byte payloads); BLE

vendors.notes: ADAU1452 based. Not in the requested list but relevant: cheap Chinese DSP amps share a few OEM platforms; one protocol driver can cover many brands. Warning in repo: never send WRITE_DSP to CH0.
